desc: 5-ft ridge section of a Japanese kawara roof (noshi stack under a round cap)

design: A Japanese late-Edo KAWARA roof RIDGE module: a stack of FIVE flat noshi-gawara ridge tiles laid in neat horizontal layers along its length (each layer a crisp thin dark line of shadow), plastered at its foot onto a row of small grey tile ends, and crowned along its whole top by ONE continuous ROUND cap tile (kanmuri-gawara, a half cylinder). Matte smoky silver-grey fired clay, cool blue-grey to pewter. It is ONE straight 5-ft MODULE of a roof ridge, seen from the side at a three-quarter angle: a LONG horizontal bar about three times as long as it is tall, its long axis running LEFT-RIGHT across the picture. Both ENDS are cut clean and flat (square), so copies butt end to end into one continuous ridge; the underside is a shallow inverted V (it sits astride the roof peak). No end ornament, no roof slopes attached.
